name: L9110S dual-channel motor driver
description: Two ASIC L9110 push-pull bridge chips on one small board: drives two small DC motors (or one 4-wire bipolar stepper) forwards, backwards or stopped, 800 mA continuous per channel (1.5-2 A peak), with built-in clamp diodes. One supply of 2.5-12 V feeds both the chips and the motors; the inputs accept 3.3 V or 5 V logic. Sold as: L9110S 2-channel H-bridge motor driver module (HG7881-style 29 x 23 mm board, 6-pin header B-IA B-IB GND VCC A-IA A-IB, screw terminals MOTOR-A and MOTOR-B).
eli5: Lets your board make two small motors spin forwards or backwards, using the motor battery's power rather than the board's own pins.

pins.name: B-IA
pins.description: Motor B input A (high = OA side driven; PWM for speed)

pins.name: GND
pins.description: Ground: common to the motor supply and the microcontroller

pins.name: VCC
pins.description: Chip and motor supply, 2.5-12 V (powers the motors, so use a supply that can deliver the motor current)

pins.name: A-IA
pins.description: Motor A input A (input high >= 2.5 V, so 3.3 V GPIOs work)

supplierQuery: L9110S 2 channel H-bridge motor driver module
buildNotes: Logic table (L9110 datasheet): IA high / IB low = forward, IA low / IB high = reverse, both low or both high = both outputs low (motor stopped).
There is no enable pin: for speed, PWM the input that is high and keep the other low (or PWM both pins and set one to 0 %).
VCC feeds the motors directly (2.5-12 V). Use a separate battery or supply for the motors and join its GND to the microcontroller GND; do not run motors from the board's 3V3 pin.
Each channel is rated 800 mA continuous (1.5-2 A peak). Small hobby/toy gear motors only; stalled motors can exceed this and overheat the SOP-8 chips.
Inputs need >= 2.5 V for high and <= 0.7 V for low, so 3.3 V and 5 V microcontrollers both drive them directly.
Vendors label the inputs B-IA/B-IB/A-IA/A-IB or B-1A/B-1B/A-1A/A-1B; they are the same pins in the same order.

driver.code:
# L9110S dual-channel motor driver module (two ASIC L9110 chips), MicroPython driver for ONE channel.
# Make one L9110S object per motor: motor A = A-IA, A-IB; motor B = B-IA, B-IB.
# Logic table from the L9110 datasheet (IA, IB -> OA, OB):
#   H, L -> H, L   forward
#   L, H -> L, H   reverse
#   L, L -> L, L   both outputs low (motor stopped, braked)
#   H, H -> L, L   both outputs low (motor stopped, braked)
# The board has no enable pin: speed is set by PWM on the input that is high.
# Inputs are TTL/CMOS: high >= 2.5 V, low <= 0.7 V, so 3.3 V GPIOs drive them directly.
from machine import Pin, PWM


class L9110S:
    def __init__(self, ia, ib, freq=1000):
        """ia, ib: GPIO numbers wired to the channel's IA and IB pins (A-IA/A-IB or B-IA/B-IB)."""
        self.ia = PWM(Pin(ia, Pin.OUT), freq=freq, duty_u16=0)
        self.ib = PWM(Pin(ib, Pin.OUT), freq=freq, duty_u16=0)

    @staticmethod
    def _duty(speed):
        speed = max(0, min(100, speed))
        return speed * 65535 // 100

    def forward(self, speed=100):
        """IA driven (PWM duty = speed %), IB low -> OA high, OB low."""
        self.ib.duty_u16(0)
        self.ia.duty_u16(self._duty(speed))

    def reverse(self, speed=100):
        """IA low, IB driven (PWM duty = speed %) -> OA low, OB high."""
        self.ia.duty_u16(0)
        self.ib.duty_u16(self._duty(speed))

    def stop(self):
        """Both inputs low -> both outputs low: the motor stops."""
        self.ia.duty_u16(0)
        self.ib.duty_u16(0)

    def deinit(self):
        self.stop()
        self.ia.deinit()
        self.ib.deinit()

example.code:
import time
from l9110s import L9110S

# Motor A on A-IA / A-IB.
motor = L9110S({A_IA}, {A_IB})
while True:
    motor.forward()
    print('motor A forward')
    time.sleep(1)
    motor.stop()
    print('motor A stopped')
    time.sleep(1)
